children: By Caitlin McCabe and Sam Goldfarb

Treasury yields are rising to new highs after investors expressed disappointment that the Treasury Department's expanded bond buyback program wasn't larger. The 10-year yield approached 4.85%, its highest level since 2023, after Treasury said it would buy back up to $6 billion in longer-term debt. Some expected a larger buyback, which could have calmed yields down a bit more.

Bessent had "set expectations really high" when he had emphasized last month that doubling the size of buybacks to $4 billion per operation was the minimum that he could do, said Leah Traub, a fixed-income portfolio manager at Lord Abbett.
U.S. stock indexes are trending lower, with the Dow leading losses again. It would be the third straight decline for major U.S. benchmarks.

In energy, oil crossed the $100-a-barrel threshold this morning after a fresh round of strikes in the Middle East. The U.S. destroyed four Iranian tankers in the Gulf of Oman and one near Kharg Island yesterday, following attempts by Tehran to strike American warships.

Traders have become accustomed to hundred-dollar oil since Washington's conflict with Tehran started, but it has been a while. The last time Brent crude futures hit $100 was in July, before slipping below $80 in early August. Today's spike puts prices about $20 higher in just a few weeks.
